title: MCP Server & Tools
lead: Around 29 Model-Context-Protocol tools that let an agent live inside the palace.
summary: The MCP server (mcp_server.py, 2,869 lines) exposes the entire palace read/write/knowledge-graph interface as JSON-RPC tools for Claude Code and Claude Desktop. It implements stdio protection to block transitive dependencies from corrupting the JSON-RPC stream, cache invalidation to detect external database writes, aggressive retry logic for ChromaDB stale handles, and a write-ahead log for audit trails. The 29 tools span palace reads (list/search/traverse), writes (add/update/delete drawers, sync), knowledge graph mutations (add/query/invalidate facts with temporal filtering), tunnels (cross-wing connections), diaries (agent journals in AAAK), and maintenance (reconnect, hook settings).

concepts.definition: Model Context Protocol — a JSON-RPC 2.0 request/response interface over stdio for Claude Code and Claude Desktop to invoke tools without network round-trips.
Redirection of stdout and file-descriptor level (os.dup2) before heavy imports to prevent transitive dependencies (chromadb, onnxruntime) from writing banners/errors that corrupt JSON-RPC payloads.
Detection of external writes via inode + mtime checks on chroma.sqlite3, forcing ChromaDB client/collection rebuild to prevent stale HNSW indices.
One-shot retry pattern in _call_kg for sqlite3.ProgrammingError when a KnowledgeGraph handle is closed mid-operation (race between tool call and reconnect).
JSONL audit trail at ~/.mempalace/wal/write_log.jsonl recording all drawer/KG mutations with content redaction for review and rollback.
Compressed memory format using entity codes (ALC, JOR), emotion markers (*warm*, *fierce*), and pipe-separated fields for agents to write dense diary entries.
Explicit cross-wing connection (stored in tunnels.json) linking rooms that relate across projects/domains, complementing implicit graph edges from rooms spanning multiple wings.
Daemon watchdog thread that exits the MCP process after MEMPALACE_MCP_IDLE_HOURS (default 8h) with no requests, releasing ChromaDB file handles on Windows.

symbols.name: tool_status
symbols.role: Palace overview: total drawers, wing/room breakdown, protocol version, AAAK spec, HNSW capacity probe result.

symbols.name: tool_search
symbols.role: Semantic + keyword search with wing/room filters, max_distance threshold, query sanitization, vector-disabled fallback.

symbols.name: tool_add_drawer
symbols.role: File verbatim content with duplicate check, chunking for oversized content, idempotency probe, WAL logging.

symbols.name: tool_kg_query
symbols.role: Query knowledge graph for entity's relationships (outgoing/incoming/both) with optional as_of temporal filter.

symbols.name: tool_diary_write
symbols.role: Agent diary entry in AAAK format, optional topic/wing, timestamp-based id for append-only semantics.

symbols.name: tool_reconnect
symbols.role: Force cache invalidation and ChromaDB/KG reconnect after external writes, clear HNSW divergence flag.

symbols.name: _get_client
symbols.role: Return cached ChromaDB PersistentClient with inode/mtime staleness detection and HNSW capacity probe.

symbols.name: _call_kg
symbols.role: Wrap KG operation with one-shot retry on sqlite3.ProgrammingError (closed database during reconnect).

symbols.name: TOOLS
symbols.role: MCP protocol registry mapping tool names to {description, input_schema, handler} — 29 tools total.

symbols.name: handle_request
symbols.role: JSON-RPC 2.0 dispatcher: routes initialize/ping/tools/list/tools/call, validates params, catches TypeError for arity errors.

symbols.name: _wal_log
symbols.role: Append JSONL audit entry to ~/.mempalace/wal/write_log.jsonl with operation, params (redacted), timestamp.

symbols.name: _vector_disabled
symbols.role: Flag set when hnsw_capacity_status detects divergence; gates vector search to BM25-only fallback.

surprises.title: Transitive Dependency Stdio Corruption Blocker
surprises.detail: ChromaDB → ONNX/posthog and other transitive dependencies write JSON banners to stdout at C level (not via Python), breaking the JSON-RPC parser in Claude Desktop. The solution (os.dup2 before imports) is nonobvious — redirecting sys.stdout alone doesn't catch fd-level writes from C libraries. The workaround must happen at import time, not in main().

surprises.title: ChromaDB Silent Truncation at 10K Rows
surprises.detail: _fetch_all_metadata paginates col.get() in 1000-row batches (line 621) because ChromaDB silently truncates results at 10K without raising. Warm metadata cache only applies when where=None (line 649) — filtered queries always paginate fresh to avoid stale subsets.

surprises.title: One-Shot Retry on KG Close Instead of Loop
surprises.detail: _call_kg retries at most once on sqlite3.ProgrammingError (line 282) rather than spinning — a second close is a lost race, not a transient. The tradeoff is that reconnect-during-handler still fails on second attempt, but avoids hung loops (line 263).

surprises.title: HNSW Capacity Probe Before Client Open
surprises.detail: _refresh_vector_disabled_flag() (line 350) reads pure sqlite + pickle metadata from chromadb's segment files to detect index divergence WITHOUT opening a PersistentClient. This avoids segfaults on load (issue #1222) by gating the chromadb client open. The probe is pure filesystem read with zero chromadb interaction.

surprises.title: Agent Diaries Normalized to Lowercase for Case-Insensitive Reads
surprises.detail: agent_name is normalized to .lower() at write (line 1617) and read (line 1745) so 'Claude', 'claude', 'CLAUDE' all resolve to the same diary. This breaks pre-fix mixed-case entries unless repaired, but keeps future reads robust (issue #1243). Filters on wing + room='diary' + agent (lines 1758-1760).

designDecisions.rationale: Provides audit trail for detecting memory poisoning and enables review/rollback without touching the vector index. Content is redacted to avoid logging sensitive user data. Local-first storage (CLAUDE.md) means the log is operator-accessible and never auto-purged — trust boundary is the user's machine.

KnowledgeGraph can close between _get_kg() and op(kg) call during reconnect. One-shot retry is simpler than RWLock + readers/writers semantics and preserves the contract that reconnect cleanly resets state without leaking handles. Spinning/hung loops are worse than a single failure (CLAUDE.md performance budgets).

designDecisions.decision: Inode + mtime Staleness Detection Over File Watches
designDecisions.rationale: Stateless detection works across platforms (including Windows FAT), requires no background threads, and handles both full rebuilds (inode) and in-place modifications (mtime). Avoids filesystem watch API complexity and platform-specific TOCTOU races. Cheap (stat syscall) to run before every chromadb touch.

designDecisions.decision: Metadata Cache with 5-Second TTL Over Always-Fresh
designDecisions.rationale: Metadata changes on every write (status, list_wings/rooms, get_taxonomy all call _get_cached_metadata). Always-fresh would require paginating 1000+ drawers on every read. 5-second TTL balances freshness with latency; cache is invalidated immediately on writes (lines 1194, 1228, 1268, 1459, 1310).

designDecisions.decision: Opt-In Eager Warmup Instead of Blocking Main
designDecisions.rationale: Cold ONNX load (5-30s) + HNSW segment load can exceed MCP client timeout (issue #1495). Eager warmup pays both costs at startup, but is opt-in (MEMPALACE_EAGER_WARMUP env var) to preserve default startup latency. Users with large existing palaces set the flag; fresh installations don't pay the cost.

searchDoc.title: MCP Server & Tools
searchDoc.summary: The MemPalace MCP server exposes around 29 JSON-RPC tools that let Claude Code and Claude Desktop read and write the palace, mutate the temporal knowledge graph, manage cross-wing tunnels, and append agent diaries.
searchDoc.body: The MemPalace MCP server (mcp_server.py, 2,869 lines) exposes the entire palace read, write, and knowledge-graph interface as roughly 29 JSON-RPC 2.0 tools for Claude Code and Claude Desktop, communicating over stdio without network round-trips. main() restores the real stdout, configures UTF-8 on Windows, starts the idle watchdog, then loops reading JSON-RPC requests from stdin. handle_request() routes initialize, ping, tools/list, and tools/call methods, validates parameter types against each tool's input schema, whitelists unknown arguments, and writes responses to stdout. A central design concern is stdio protection: before any imports, the module saves the real stdout fd via os.dup, redirects fd 1 to fd 2 (stderr), and sets sys.stdout to sys.stderr, preventing transitive dependencies like chromadb and onnxruntime from writing C-level banners that would corrupt the JSON-RPC stream. _restore_stdout undoes both the fd and Python-level redirects in main. Cache management uses inode plus mtime staleness detection on chroma.sqlite3: _get_client compares current st_ino and st_mtime against cached values, and an inode change (full rebuild) or mtime change (external write greater than ten milliseconds) triggers a ChromaDB client rebuild. Before opening the client, _refresh_vector_disabled_flag probes HNSW capacity via a pure sqlite and pickle read, never touching chromadb, so the issue 1222 divergence flag is set before segment load to avoid segfaults. Knowledge graph operations run through _call_kg, which captures the canonical KG path once via realpath and normcase and retries once on sqlite3.ProgrammingError when a handle is closed mid-operation during reconnect. Write tools log to a write-ahead log at the home mempalace wal directory before mutating, with content, query, and entry fields redacted via a frozenset of keys. tool_add_drawer detects idempotency by probing drawer_id and the last chunk id, and chunks oversized content into a single batched all-or-nothing upsert. Metadata is cached for five seconds and invalidated on writes; _fetch_all_metadata paginates in 1000-row batches because ChromaDB silently truncates at 10K rows. Diary tools normalize agent names to lowercase for case-insensitive reads. An idle watchdog exits after MEMPALACE_MCP_IDLE_HOURS, default eight hours, to release ChromaDB file handles on Windows, and opt-in eager warmup pre-loads the embedder to avoid timeout errors on large palaces. Tool categories are Read seven, Write five, KG six, Tunnels six, Diaries two, and Settings three.
